newsitem.title: NORWAY: Smedvig wins U.S. drilling contract.
newsitem.headline: Smedvig wins U.S. drilling contract.

text.p: Norwegian offshore group Smedvig ASA said on Thursday it had signed a letter of intent with Shell Deepwater Development Inc. of the United States for a long-term deep water drilling contract in the Gulf of Mexico.
The assignment will run for five years and has an estimated value of 2.1 billion crowns.
Smedvig said the deal was a breakthrough first drilling assignment for the company in the U.S. market.
Shell Deepwater Development Inc. is part of the Shell Oil group, which itself is affiliate of the Royal/Dutch Shell Group.

Smedvig said the contract was based on using a newbuild multipurpose shuttle tanker (MST) from Statoil Shipping & Maritime Technology, a part of state Norwegian oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS.

Smedvig will outfit the vessel as a drill ship and will commission and operate the unit, which is expected to cost $280-$290 million. Smedvig ans Statoil will each have an equal financial interest in the vessel.
The MST is due to be ready for operations in the second quarter 1999.
